Episode 254. The Egos of the Sun God (7)
As a giant blade shot up from the hull of the flagship Sarah, the advance of the Golden Fleet began.
At a speed unbelievable for a flying ship, the flagship Sarah plunged its blade into the central part of the Tower of Story like a descending hawk.

A shockwave and a deafening roar erupted, and fragments of the pure white mineral that composed the tower scattered. The fragments that shot up between Jin and Kelliark could not withstand the heat and instantly dispersed into particles.
With the blade relentlessly pushing in, Kelliark could not shake off Jin at all.
'I... Kelliark Zipfel. Cannot even handle Jin Runcandel, let alone Chiron...!'

His entire life, he had been overshadowed by the figure of Chiron Runcandel, remaining in the position of second best. Although the Zipfel faction itself was undoubtedly the strongest, Kelliark as an individual had never been so.
The patriarch of the Zipfel, who had possessed so much, enjoyed so much, and ruled over so much, had, in fact, always harbored an inferiority complex.
That inferiority complex, which had only ever flared up when facing Chiron, was now rearing its head in front of the young Jin.

“Shut up, Jin Runcandel. Do you think you can have anything you want when this fight is over? Do you think the world will become peaceful? Nothing will change. Nothing! Only the Origin Stone, only complete control, can change things. Not the struggles you bastards prattle on about!”
Pshht-!
A drop of blood flew from Kelliark's forehead. The wound left on his forehead by Bradamante was curved just like a smile mocking him.
“Is that so? Then all you have to do is defeat me and prove the words you just spat out. But you can't, can you? Just as you have never once defeated my father.”
Hwaaaaak-!

The Eternal Flames resonated with the flagship Sarah, spreading an even thicker blue flame. The ceiling and walls of the tower's central part had now all melted away, revealing the golden-dyed scenery outside, and blue flames were billowing in all directions.
“Keuk...!”

Kelliark grunted, brushing off the blue flames that had stuck to his shoulder and arm. Sheenu's unique crimson flames were offsetting the blue flames. However, the speed at which they were being offset was not very fast.
It was because he was being overwhelmed. Jin, who had ascended to the state of a Genesis Knight, and the flagship Sarah, which amplified his power, had now surpassed even a divinity like Sheenu.
“How amusing, Kelliark. Is this all you have? After committing such horrific atrocities to become the one and only god, without the Origin Stone, you are nothing but an old fossil.”
“Keoheok!”

A Soul-Slaying Slash following a light-speed thrust; two sword-auras struck Kelliark's body. Although they were blocked by a hastily raised shield, a significant impact was transmitted, and Kelliark spat out blood as his knees buckled.
To avoid the ensuing consecutive strikes, Kelliark threw his body and rolled on the floor. It was a laughable sight, but if he had been even a little late, his head would have been severed.
'The gap can't be this large... but why...!'
For Kelliark, it was incomprehensible.
Although he had not reached the state of a Genesis Knight directly like Jin, he had fused with Sheenu and obtained a corresponding power.

He had firmly believed so. When he conquered the Demon Realm, when he returned to his family and reclaimed the position of patriarch, Kelliark had always overwhelmed those who resisted based on that power.
Suddenly, the shocking and miserable feeling of just how much he had relied on the 'Origin Stone' was creeping up on him.
'Killing Kelliark is not the problem.'

Jin, on the other hand, was gaining insight into this situation even while continuing his relentless pressure. This was not the time to be intoxicated by the emotion of finally being able to finish off the leader of the Zipfel.
'The one to truly be wary of is not this old fossil, but Malugia. I must grasp what that ego of the Sun God was thinking when she created this situation.'
Kragos, who was facing Vahn and the Plutonian Golden Fleet outside the Tower of Story, had awoken by Malugia's will.
He had received Malugia's authority and become stronger than his original self, and had even supported Kelliark when he struck Dante.
It meant that the one who had planned this game was not Kelliark in the first place.

'According to our hypothesis, Malugia is waiting for the right time for the destruction of all dimensions. And to ruin other dimensions... she would first need to summon them. Or open a path to them.'
Sgeok-!
After severing three of Kelliark's fingers, Jin dodged the spatial explosion that followed as a counterattack and naturally surveyed his surroundings.
Bligiet, Nepdol, Kragos, Focal.
Suddenly, the fact that there were four egos of the Sun God gathered in this place stood out in his mind. If one were to assume that Malugia was hiding somewhere, that made five.

'If the immense Sun energies of those five were to be endlessly emitted like this, couldn't that alone have some effect on other dimensions? And based on that influence, Malugia could be plotting something.'
That thought occurred to him in a flash.
Furthermore, Silkia Arcia, who possessed a dimensional travel ability powerful enough to be compared to the Sun God Focal, was also present here.
It was just a hypothesis, but there was no harm in being careful.

“From now on, Lord Focal, please refrain from using your Sun energy as much as possible. Sister Vahn and the companions can pressure Kragos more than enough on their own. I will also be joining them soon after finishing off Kelliark. And Lord Bluggiet, Nepdol, and Silkia, it would be best for you to retreat outside the front lines and be on standby.”
As Jin communicated once more after slamming Kelliark, Focal instantly understood his intention with her divine insight.
[Jin is right. Since Malugia has not yet revealed herself, we cannot know what consequences the excessive use of Sun energy might bring.]
The best outcome for the coalition was to finish off the enemies as quickly as possible and leave the battlefield. Before any other variables or incidents could occur.
Now, Kelliark was barely holding on against Jin, and more than half of the remaining Zipfel mages had already died.
Keydart Hall and the old patriarchs of the Zipfel who had been resurrected from hell were fighting valiantly in their own way, but they were having no effect on the tide of the war.
“We must save Lady Elona. No, secure her! Encircle Ragal more tightly. So that bastard cannot escape!”
It was Veradin's voice.
He couldn't bring himself to say they must 'save' Elona. In the coalition, in this world, there were too many people who had lost their families, lost their friends, lost their loves by her power.
Still, the reason he said they must secure Elona without killing her was because of the feeling that she and he must, in some way, atone for the rest of their lives.

On the other hand, he showed not a shred of interest in his father, Kelliark Zipfel, who was on the verge of death. It was because he could not forgive anything about Kelliark. He was a monster who did not even deserve to atone.
The only things Veradin was focused on were Elona Zipfel and the living golems created based on his own ego, Almatia and Kun.

They, at least, deserved the chance for atonement, just like him. In fact, they deserved the chance more than he did. Because at that time, the sole decision-maker of the Zipfel was none other than himself.
“Brother Kaio.”
“Yes, Sister Goddess of Battle.”
“Brother, you kill that bastard named Ragal and secure Elona Zipfel. It seems that bastard has been continuously applying poison to Elona Zipfel's body.”
Only Vahn had been able to notice that fact. It was a detail that Jin, who was fighting Kelliark while also commanding the overall situation, had missed.
“Understood.”
“Brothers Linpa and Baltirock, you go and find those named Almatia and Kun.”
“Yes, brother!”

The Battle Kings who had been fighting Kragos together were pulling out according to the order. However, even as some of the Battle Kings withdrew, Kragos could not feel any breathing room. Even though the Sun energy from Focal that had been pouring down on him had also faded.
Rather, it felt as if Vahn's blade was getting closer and closer. It was because Vahn and Murakan had that much more of a grasp and understanding of Kragos's power.
Furthermore, there wasn't much time. Soon, Jin would cut down Kelliark and join the fight here, and Luna's crimson sword was also breaking through the Sun energy to join them.

[How interesting, mortal who inherited my power. Bligiet, Nepdol, and even Beltian. Those fools must have been very flustered when they first saw you. Originally, you should not be able to attack us...]
Kragos said, gripping his sword. Unlike when he had struck Dante, there was no trace of leisure or laughter on his face.
[But you will never be able to do so against Malugia, mortal Vahn. She has now finished almost all her preparations. Preparations for the apocalypse.]

“What is this bastard babbling about? It seems you'd fit right in working for us next to Beltian, so struggle moderately. If you don't want to get beaten to a pulp and look pathetic like your other brothers.”
Murakan answered for her and exhaled his breath. Kragos struck away the breath and emitted his Sun energy, but he could not break through Vahn's Plutonian Domination Sword, which had just begun.
Just like that day when the coalition first completed the Golden Fleet and struck the Tower of Story.
The battlefield was divided left and right, filling up with the strengthened Plutonian Domination Sword and Eternal Flames, resonating with the Golden Fleet.

As the energies of the two Genesis Knights, Jin and Vahn, grew larger, for some reason, the golden sea that had been churning violently seemed to calm down. As if that sight was of some comfort to the lives that had been unjustly turned into golden water.
For Kragos, and for Kelliark.
It seemed they did not have the ability to turn the situation around on their own. Kelliark, in particular, was now looking around with eyes completely filled with despair.

It was because he could not grasp from where Jin's sword would fly in. He was slammed into various parts of the Tower of Story' central area, eventually falling to the lower levels of the tower, and was panting for breath in a pit-like darkness.
'Where are you... from where will you come!'
Soon, the moment Kelliark raised his head, scattering crimson flames in all directions.
He came face to face with a single sword falling on his head like a thunderbolt. That sword had already completely bisected the central part of the Tower of Story as it fell towards Kelliark.

The blade, after severing Kelliark's right arm and shoulder which had been holding the staff, was emitting a massive sword-aura that cut through to the very bottom of the Tower of Story in a single breath.
